summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled 'Book 12 — part 71') describing a spring afternoon when Lexy and Houseman walk by a stream, skipping stones and talking casually. Houseman reveals he is a twenty-six-year-old from Baltimore working on a cargo steamer, and the two feel a growing bond. At sunset Mrs. Royce, watching from the kitchen, concludes Houseman is the one for Lexy, while George Grey, in the sitting room, is privately suffering. The passage ends with Lexy introducing Houseman to George as Caroline Enderby's fiancé.
one_line: A spring-afternoon excerpt from a novel in which Lexy and Houseman bond by a stream while George Grey silently suffers.
key_facts: Houseman skipped stones with skill and earnest attention beside the stream while Lexy watched minnows in the limpid water.
Houseman said he was from Baltimore and that his people wanted him to go into the navy.
Houseman's father and grandfather were both in the navy, but Houseman said 'Too cut and dried!' and is on a cargo steamer now.
Houseman was twenty-six, had two brothers in the navy and three married sisters, and both parents were living.
Lexy regarded Houseman as 'a comrade and an ally without an equal.'
At sunset Houseman found nothing better to say than that he was hungry, and Lexy replied 'So am I!'
Mrs. Royce saw Lexy and Houseman strolling side by side from the kitchen window.
Mrs. Royce concluded, 'He's the one!' after hearing Lexy mention clam chowder and Houseman's knowledge of oysters.
Mrs. Royce began making a superb chocolate cake and hummed a song about a young man on Springfield Mountain who killed a 'pesky sarpent.'
George Grey sat in the sitting room smoking and pretending to read, never turning a page.
George Grey looked fastidiously neat, self-possessed, and a little haughty, but was suffering horribly in spirit.
Lexy held out her hand to George Grey and searched his face with an anxious and friendly glance.
Lexy introduced Houseman as 'Caroline Enderby's fiancé.'
The excerpt also includes an unrelated sentence about 2013, when Caleb saw the original 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' painting up close after waiting in line for hours.
